english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated wounding / grievous bodily harm
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and maliciously

(A)_[wounded **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[inflicted grievous bodily harm to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_

and the offence was

(C)_[racially]_
(D)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 29(1)(a) and (2) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
unlawfully and maliciously
wounded a person OR
inflict grievous bodily harm on a person
and the offence was racially/religiously aggravated
within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) If, on trial on indictments of a person charged with this offence, the jury find him not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
